Multi-row label placement engine

Source: R/smart-stack.R
smart_stack.Rd

smart_stack() assigns a set of label boxes (each with an axis position positions and a width widths, both in npc) to one of n rows (n columns for a y axis) so that every label can be drawn, labels within a row do not overlap, and each label stays as close as possible to its original position. It is the placement engine behind guide_axis_smart() and can also be used on its own.

Usage

smart_stack(
  positions,
  widths,
  n,
  range = c(0, 1),
  extend = 0,
  padding = 0,
  priority = NULL
)

Arguments

positions

Numeric vector of axis positions (npc, 0..1) of the label boxes. Does not need to be sorted.

widths

Numeric vector of box widths (npc), the same length as positions.

n

Positive integer, the number of rows (columns for a y axis). It also sets the total capacity.

range

Numeric vector of length 2, the drawable range of the axis, default c(0, 1).

extend

Non-negative scalar, how far labels may stick out of range (0.02 widens the axis span by 0.02 on each side); same meaning as the argument of the same name in guide_axis_smart().

padding

Non-negative scalar, the minimum gap required between neighbouring boxes in the same row, in the same unit as positions (npc).

priority

NULL (default, all labels equally important) or a numeric vector the same length as positions. Larger values are kept first; when space runs out the low-priority labels are dropped.

Value

A data.frame with one row per input box, in input order, with columns:

  • index: the input index (1..length(positions));

  • row: the assigned row (1..n); NA for dropped labels;

  • start, end: the left and right end of the placed box (npc);

  • center: the centre of the placed box (npc);

  • shown: logical, whether the label should be drawn.

Details

The algorithm has three steps:

  1. Usable range: range is widened on both sides by extend * diff(range) to give lim; boxes wider than diff(lim) can never fit and are dropped.

  2. Row assignment: boxes are processed from the highest to the lowest priority (larger priority first; ties by position, then by index). Each box goes to the row that currently carries the least load among the rows that still have capacity (load = sum of widths in the row plus the padding gaps it needs), so with equal priorities the labels alternate between rows along the axis (water-filling balance). Labels that fit in no row are dropped (shown = FALSE).

  3. Packing inside a row: within a row the boxes keep their axis order by centre position; each box is inflated by padding / 2 on both sides, the packing algorithm removes the overlaps, and the boxes are shrunk back, so neighbouring labels in a row end up exactly padding apart. An order-preserving projection clamps the centres into the usable range before inflation, so the result never leaves lim.

  • Every box with shown = TRUE satisfies lim[1] <= start < end <= lim[2]; within a row, after sorting by start, start[i+1] >= end[i] + padding (equality holds when no edge clamping kicks in).

  • The order inside a row follows the box centres, i.e. the axis order.

  • Row assignment depends on priority and load balancing only and is deterministic: the same input always gives the same output, with no random numbers involved.

  • The function guarantees "drawn means not overlapping", but it never squeezes a label below its widths; labels that do not fit are dropped (shown = FALSE).

  • When there are many labels and the n rows do not provide enough capacity, the lowest-priority labels are dropped first; among equal priorities the labels nearest the left end of the axis are processed first.

See also

smart_align(), box_arrange()

Examples

# six labels spread along the axis in 2 rows: alternate, barely moved
pos <- seq(0.1, 0.9, length.out = 6)
smart_stack(pos, widths = rep(0.08, 6), n = 2)
#>   index row start  end center shown
#> 1     1   1  0.06 0.14   0.10  TRUE
#> 2     2   2  0.22 0.30   0.26  TRUE
#> 3     3   1  0.38 0.46   0.42  TRUE
#> 4     4   2  0.54 0.62   0.58  TRUE
#> 5     5   1  0.70 0.78   0.74  TRUE
#> 6     6   2  0.86 0.94   0.90  TRUE

# three labels crowded around 0.5 still do not overlap in 3 rows
smart_stack(c(0.48, 0.5, 0.52), widths = rep(0.2, 3), n = 3)
#>   index row start  end center shown
#> 1     1   1  0.38 0.58   0.48  TRUE
#> 2     2   2  0.40 0.60   0.50  TRUE
#> 3     3   3  0.42 0.62   0.52  TRUE

# when space runs out, priority decides what is dropped
smart_stack(
  positions = rep(0.5, 5), widths = rep(0.4, 5), n = 1,
  priority = c(1, 5, 3, 4, 2)
)
#>   index row start end center shown
#> 1     1  NA   0.3 0.7    0.5 FALSE
#> 2     2   1   0.1 0.5    0.3  TRUE
#> 3     3  NA   0.3 0.7    0.5 FALSE
#> 4     4   1   0.5 0.9    0.7  TRUE
#> 5     5  NA   0.3 0.7    0.5 FALSE
